examples.text: Что это тут за ужасный запах?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он бы, наверное, сказал именно так.
examples.trans: He would probably have put it just like this.

examples.text: Машина так и стоит во дворе.
examples.trans: The car just stands there in the courtyard.

examples.trans: What smells so strange in here?

examples.trans: What smells so strange in here?
It smells bad here.
The coffee smells good.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'suspicion' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.text: Сеня, ты подозрения от себя отводишь?
examples.trans: Senya, are you deflecting suspicion from yourself?
This doesn't raise suspicion.
I have a suspicion.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'from' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: Then take the keys to the car.

examples.text: Он будет ждать гадости от вас.

examples.text: Сеня, ты подозрения от себя отводишь?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Два шефа ведут между собой бои.
examples.trans: Two chefs wage battles between themselves.
You should not behave like that.

examples.text: Шеф, вы ведёте себя как ребёнок.
examples.trans: Chef, you are behaving like a child.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (root 'водить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to yourself'.

examples.text: Сеня, ты подозрения от себя отводишь?
examples.trans: Senya, are you deflecting suspicion from yourself?

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian interj meaning 'oh', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, what just happened?
Oh, it seems the elevator has stopped.
Oh, look!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to seem', forming an aspectual pair with 'показаться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Oh, it seems the elevator has stopped.

examples.text: Кажется, я нашла нам нового сомелье.
examples.trans: It seems I have found us a new sommelier.
I think he's right.

examples.trans: Oh, it seems the elevator has stopped.

остановиться.gloss: to stop, to come to a halt

meanings.en: to stop, to come to a halt
meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to stop', forming an aspectual pair with 'останавливаться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Oh, it seems the elevator has stopped.

examples.text: Он только начал бояться, а ты остановился!
examples.trans: He just started getting scared, and you stopped!
Has the bleeding stopped yet?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('not') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Женщина, не отвлекай, я сейчас проигрываю!
examples.trans: Woman, do not distract me, I am losing right now!

examples.text: Ты полгода резину поменять не можешь.
examples.trans: You have not been able to change the tires for half a year.
You have not finished anything at all!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to panic'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Do not panic ahead of time.

examples.text: Вика, не паникуй, я уже несу горячее блюдо.
examples.trans: Vika, do not panic, I am already carrying the hot dish.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('we') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: А что нам со старой мебелью делать?
examples.trans: And what should we do with the old furniture?
Of course, we finished it a long time ago.
And you, create an atmosphere for us.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'stuck', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Vika, do not panic, we are stuck.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, мы тут в лифте застряли.
examples.trans: Hello, we are stuck in the elevator here.
Hello, we have been stuck in here for a long time.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('well') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Max, well, what is this?

examples.text: Ну, вы у меня ещё попляшете!
examples.trans: Well, you will pay for this yet!
Well, do not get so worked up, chef.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Вика, давай я всё сам сделаю.
examples.trans: Vika, let me do everything myself.
We will see how you do that.

examples.text: Что же надо с ним сделать?
examples.trans: What should we do to him?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('but') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Макс, я же тебя просила починить.
examples.trans: Max, I asked you to fix it.
Yes, of course, and just when will that be?

examples.text: Мне же каждый день звонили отсюда.
examples.trans: People called me from here every day.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('at least') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well, do something at least!
Give me just one.
At least a little.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('something') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: Well, do something at least!
Fine, I will think of something right now.
Say something.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты просто открутил эту штуку!
examples.trans: And you simply unscrewed this thing!

examples.text: А что нам со старой мебелью делать?
examples.trans: And what should we do with the old furniture?

examples.text: А вы закончили вашу дурацкую войну?
examples.trans: And have you finished your foolish war?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('I') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: I will buy a new one later and screw it on.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Ты полгода резину поменять не можешь.
examples.trans: You have not been able to change the tires for half a year.

examples.text: А что я тут могу сделать?
examples.trans: And what can I do in here?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: I do not know myself yet.

examples.text: И это всё, что ты знаешь?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Эй, это что у тебя такое?

examples.text: У вас на кухне живая змея!

examples.text: Ну, вы у меня ещё попляшете!
examples.trans: Well, you will pay for this yet!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'man', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я в этом доме и мужчина, и женщина.

examples.trans: I do not know, you are the man here.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('all right') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Fine, come inside quietly.
Fine, I will think of something right now.
Fine, be ready by evening.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.text: Женщина, не отвлекай, я сейчас проигрываю!
examples.trans: Woman, do not distract me, I am losing right now!
Oh, what just happened?
All right, I will play for you right now.

придумать.gloss: to think up, to come up with

meanings.en: to think up, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (root 'думать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to think up', forming an aspectual pair with 'придумывать'.

examples.trans: Can you imagine what German thought up?
Fine, I will think of something right now.
You came up with this yourself!

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian interj meaning 'hey', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Эй, это что у тебя такое?
examples.trans: Hey, what is that on your face?
Hey, is anyone out there?

examples.text: Эй, оставь её, это моя жена!
examples.trans: Hey, leave her alone, she is my wife!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Вот увидишь, вечером всё будет готово.
examples.trans: You will see, by evening everything will be ready.

examples.text: Чтобы через полчаса здесь был свет!
examples.trans: Make sure there is light in here in half an hour!

examples.text: Он будет ждать гадости от вас.
examples.trans: He will be waiting for a dirty trick from you.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'there'.

examples.trans: Vika, what are you doing in there?

examples.text: Я просто нажал там на кнопку.
examples.trans: I just pressed a button back there.
What happened in the kitchen?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('somebody') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: Hey, is anyone out there?
Somebody on the street will tell him.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'мочь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to help', forming an aspectual pair with 'помогать'.

examples.trans: Help us, please!
And not 'please help us'.
Good afternoon, how can I help you?

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('please') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, please hear me out.
Vikulya, forgive me, please.
Help us, please!
